text: The products supplied must comply with the Buy American Act, the Trade Agreement Act, and all relevant FAR and agency-specific regulations. Products must be domestic end products, meaning they are either manufactured or produced in the United States unless an exception is permitted by applicable regulations. For Commercial Off-the-Shelf (Commercial Product) items (as defined in FAR 2.101) that are sold in substantial quantities in the commercial marketplace and offered to the Government without modification, and do not include bulk cargo (as defined in 46 U.S.C. 40102(4)), the domestic content test is waived. However, for end products consisting wholly or predominantly of iron or steel (where 'predominantly' means the cost of iron and steel content exceeds 50 percent of the total cost of all components), the domestic content test applies to the iron and steel content (excluding COTS fasteners), and the cost of foreign iron and steel must be less than 5 percent. For other non-COTS items, the cost of components mined, produced, or manufactured in the United States must exceed 60 percent of the total component cost, increasing to 65 percent for items delivered in calendar years 2024 through 2028, and 75 percent for items delivered starting in calendar year 2029. Offerors must list foreign end products (including US-manufactured products that do not qualify as domestic), indicate if non-iron/steel foreign end products exceed 55 percent domestic content (except COTS), and separately list line item numbers of domestic end products containing a critical component. If domestic content percentage is unknown, select 'no'. The Government will evaluate offers in accordance with FAR Part 25.

The cost of foreign iron and steel includes but is not limited to the cost of foreign iron or steel mill products (such as bar, billet, slab, wire, plate, or sheet), castings, or forgings utilized in the manufacture of the end product and a good faith estimate of the cost of all foreign iron or steel components excluding COTS fasteners. Steel means an alloy that includes at least 50 percent iron, between 0.02 and 2 percent carbon, and may include other elements.
